conventions.convention: Complex L² consists of Lebesgue almost-everywhere classes; the inner product is ∫u conjugate(v), linear in the first argument. Weak-derivative tests use ∫uφ′=−∫Du φ without conjugation.

H¹ requires u and Du in L²; H² requires Du in H¹; H¹₀(0,L) is the H¹ closure of compactly supported smooth test functions. Endpoint values belong to the unique continuous absolutely continuous representative, rather than an arbitrary measurable representative.
The sine system and Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence start at n=1; twisted-periodic characters are indexed by all integers, with θ∈[0,2π).
Local kernel notation R₀(z) denotes (A₀−z)⁻¹, opposite in sign to the published resolvent convention (z−A)⁻¹. The square root satisfies k²=−z and Re k>0.

The delta derivative jump is u′(0+)−u′(0−)=αu(0); attraction means α<0. Separated Robin conditions are u′(0)=αu(0), u′(L)=βu(L), using coordinate derivatives at both ends rather than outward normal derivatives.
The Prüfer angle is the continuous integral-defined lift with θ(0,E)=0, u=r sin θ and u′=r cos θ; its energy derivative has endpoint denominator u(x,E)²+u′(x,E)².

The compact-resolvent eigenbasis lemma assumes infinite-dimensional H and a real resolvent point c. AC is stated for the Sobolev representative and spectral interfaces; the regular IVP and Prüfer theorem assume Countable Choice.

The finite well has V=−U on [−a,a] and zero outside, K=√(2mU)/ℏ, and strictly negative bound energies. A branch whose left endpoint equals K contributes no bound state. Barrier solutions are bounded generalized solutions, with no L² normalization.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and Countable Choice, every u∈H¹(a,b), with finite a<b, has a unique absolutely continuous representative on [a,b], satisfying u*(x)−u*(y)=∫ᵧˣu′ and |u*(x)−u*(y)|≤√|x−y|‖u′‖₂; for H², its classical first derivative is absolutely continuous with derivative class D²u.

Under AC, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the bounded-interval first- and second-order integration-by-parts identities hold, H¹₀(0,L) equals the H¹ classes with both endpoint traces zero, and the stated half-line and line identities hold with absolutely convergent integrals.

Under Countable Choice, for L>0, continuous complex V, z∈C and arbitrary initial data at x₀∈[0,L], −u″+Vu=zu has exactly one C² solution, equivalently the stated oriented Volterra solution; its Picard and first-derivative series converge uniformly on compact parameter discs, u and u′ are entire in z, and w=∂zu solves −w″+Vw−zw=u with zero initial data.
Under AC and Countable Choice, for 0<L<∞ the functions eₙ(x)=√(2/L)sin(nπx/L), n≥1, form a complete orthonormal family of complex L²(0,L).

Under AC and Countable Choice, a self-adjoint A on an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space with a compact resolvent (A−c)⁻¹ at a real c∈ρ(A) has a complete countable orthonormal eigenfamily, finite-dimensional eigenspaces, |μₙ|→∞, spectrum exactly its eigenvalue set, empty essential spectrum and compact resolvents at every resolvent point.

Under AC and Countable Choice, for z∉[0,∞) and k²=−z, Re k>0, Gz(t)=e^(−k|t|)/(2k) yields a bounded convolution operator with range exactly H²(R), both inverse identities for A₀−z, and the distributional identity (−d²/dx²−z)Gz=δ₀.

Under AC and Countable Choice, for every real α, the operator acting as −D² on the two half-lines, with global H¹, half-line H² and jump u′(0+)−u′(0−)=αu(0), is densely defined, symmetric and self-adjoint.

concerns.concern: Statement (b) says that ker(A_D−λ_n) “contains no vector orthogonal to e_n.” As written this is false: 0 belongs to the kernel and is orthogonal to e_n. Step 6.1 correctly proves ker(A_D−λ_n)=C e_n, so the intended exclusion requires “nonzero vector.”

The oscillation-layer paragraph writes ∂Eθ(L,E)=∫₀ᴸu²/(u²+u′²)>0. The cited theorem instead divides ∫₀ᴸu(t,E)²dt by the endpoint value u(L,E)²+u′(L,E)². Reading the page formula as the displayed integral of a quotient makes it false: with V=0, E=0, L=1, u(x)=x, the integral of the quotient is 1−π/4, whereas the energy derivative is 1/6. Make the endpoint denominator explicit.

Proof step 3.1 has justification tags immediately before its norm display and then continues with further displays and prose before another tag group. The complete numbered step does not occupy one paragraph with tags only at its end, contrary to the mandatory proof layout.
Steps 4.1 and 5.1 contain justification groups before subsequent displays and continuing prose. Each complete step should form one paragraph and end with its justification group.
Step 4.1 puts [step 3.1, F2, algebra] before its displayed norm bound and continues afterwards to the final tagged QED. This violates the required single-paragraph, trailing-tags layout.
Step 5.2 places tags before the first display and continues through several displays before its final tags. The complete step needs the prescribed single-paragraph layout.

Step 2.1 says the transmission asymptotics impose “the outgoing-right coefficient 0.” The stated right-hand solution is t e^(ikx), whose outgoing-right coefficient is t; it is the incoming-from-right coefficient of e^(−ikx) that is zero. The subsequent matching equations use the correct asymptotics.

Fact F2 restates the compact-resolvent eigenbasis supplier using merely “a self-adjoint operator with compact resolvent,” omitting its explicit hypothesis of compactness at a real resolvent point. Step 3.1 does supply that real point before applying F2, so the actual application is justified; the quoted interface should retain the supplier hypothesis.

The free differential identity on the full H² domain is locally extended from the supplier's Schwartz identity by symmetry and integration by parts.

The confined-momentum thought experiment preserves interval H¹ traces, the integration-by-parts signs and twisted-periodic self-adjoint domains, and explicitly carries AC and Countable Choice. Its ℏ scaling is positive and its physical conclusion remains conditional.

Checked the interval/delta model definition and the mathematical Facts of the interval, well, delta and barrier deductions.
